_meta.purpose: Doc 14 (Subject Global Parameters) encoded as SCOPE-BOUND, data-driven defaults. Each family names the exact module cohort/series/level it governs; a convention applies ONLY within that scope (authority model §3.1). Deferred assets/URLs/setup are emitted as VISIBLE 'Designer/Developer To Do:' red-note placeholders (never a hidden comment). Components owned by docs 03/04/05 are NOT re-owned — only the subject-specific CHOICE is recorded, with a cross_reference. Every class/snippet was supplied by the design team (doc 14); none are invented.

_meta.authority: TOP within a family's stated scope only; OUTSIDE that scope the Granular_Scaffold_Registry (judged at the finest reliable grouping) is authoritative. A doc-14 default is cross-checked against the registry's series house-style after applying; disagreement raises a Red Flag (never a silent override).

gold_override_policy.decided: 2026-07-12 (Chris) — the covering instruction that accompanied the 2026-07-09 doc-14 refresh.
gold_override_policy.rule: Doc-14 conventions are FORWARD-LOOKING design-team directives. The human gold library (01-Finalized_Modules_) largely PREDATES them, so the gold may not comply. For every family marked overrides_gold:true, ALL FUTURE Claude conversions adhere to the doc-14 convention EVEN WHERE the module's own human gold does not — within that family's scope, these rules sit ABOVE the LEVEL-0 own-gold target (the one recorded exception to reference/Human_Gold_Is_The_Per_Module_Target.md).
gold_override_policy.stocktake_rule: Any WT->gold->Claude stocktake, vetting run, or gate triage that finds Claude diverging from the human gold MUST first check whether the divergence matches a marked doc-14 convention in scope. A match is an INTENTIONAL, EXPECTED divergence — verdict 'DOC-14 OVERRIDE', recorded, never chased: do NOT 'fix' the converter back toward the gold on these points, and never count the divergence as a converter regression.
gold_override_policy.sibling_structure_note: Doc-14's OWN internal hierarchy is preserved: for pure page STRUCTURE where a BUILT same-series sibling disagrees with a doc-14 convention, the sibling remains the most reliable structural reference (Mode B) and the conflict is surfaced as a visible Red Flag — the conflict is never silently resolved in either direction. Chris's 2026-07-12 covering instruction governs the CONVENTIONS doc-14 states (labels, copy, fonts, red-note placeholders, carve-outs, supplied snippets, per-subject choices): on those, doc-14 wins over the gold outright.
gold_override_policy.gate_policy: How a live doc-14 emission stays regression-proof against the protected gates (which measure vs the PRE-doc-14 gold): (a) every red-note placeholder is emitted with class cv2-note IN ADDITION to the supplied inline style, so the round-72 machinery excludes it from EVERY protected gate by construction (visible form unchanged); (b) a STRUCTURAL doc-14 emission that diverges from gold ships as a NAMED 'DOC-14 DELTA' list in that round's changelog entry (rule id + affected pages), and the gates are judged net of exactly those named deltas — the documented-intentional-delta discipline, doc-14-mandated rather than editorial; (c) every family flip stays behind its `active` flag + SUBJECTPARAMS_OFF so the pre-doc-14 output is always A/B-recoverable.

_meta.note: master_enabled:false keeps the corpus output byte-identical (the mechanism is wired + demonstrable but inert by default). Turn a family live one at a time via its `active` flag + a measured, gate-proven regen round (see roadmap).

scope.label: BLL modules (all levels) — NOT the separate BLLR series (§14.9)

conventions.name: Sassoon writing font on read/interact text
conventions.detail: Any interactive/text the ākonga reads or interacts with uses the writing font refresh_sassoon_font.html. Ensure specifically: single-storey a, capital I reads as a capital I, single-storey g (these ākonga are just learning to read and write — the letters they read must match the letters they write; l and I are confusing when identical).

conventions.red_note: Designer/developer to create and embed image

conventions.name: .dropbox NOT added to .activity (BLL carve-out from constraint 43)
conventions.detail: BLL is the ONE series that does not append the `dropbox` modifier to the `.activity` wrapper; the dropbox button is still present. Scoped to BLL ONLY — it does NOT extend to the separate BLLR series (§14.9). Every other series follows constraint 43 unchanged.

conventions.name: Embedded stories = book-style carousel
conventions.detail: Story pages ONLY (no teacher notes/activities) in a carousel so it reads like a book, not scrolling down. Image URLs replaced per story.

scope.label: LS modules (XLP toolkits + XDLS exemplars + LS content)

conventions.name: .learningSupport on <html>
conventions.detail: Root tag carries class 'notranslate learningSupport' (existing CSS hook; LS always carry it). Larger font (same as LS Whakatau).

conventions.name: Terminology + first-mention brackets
conventions.detail: hoa ako (learning partner); hua ako -> check -> hoa ako; learner -> ākonga; WE/US -> you. Brackets only on the FIRST instance a term is used in a module (first mention 'hoa ako (learning partner)', plain 'hoa ako' thereafter). CONTENT rule — flag, never auto-invent.

conventions.name: Remove tab navs (lesson-based, not inquiry)
conventions.detail: LS modules are lesson-based; remove tab navs (they carry too much media). Move-on prompts go at the bottom of each page.

conventions.name: clickDrop activity layout (choicePage, per-choice icons)
conventions.detail: Activity content rows sit in col-12 col-md-8; activity wrappers off col-md-10. iconType values: learnByHeart, explain, do, compare, judge, create.

conventions.name: Action prompts = colour-coded speech-bubble character
conventions.detail: In-page action prompts are man-with-speech-bubble, colour-coded to the module, bold heading (clear about what they are looking at) + bullet-point prompting questions — NOT activity boxes. General prompting questions also go in speech bubbles.

conventions.name: Many videos/images -> slideshow with caption text
conventions.detail: When a page has many videos/images, put them in a video/image slideshow with the body text as captions, plus prompting text (e.g. 'explore the slideshow to see examples of…').

conventions.name: 6-activity pattern: one dropbox at page bottom
conventions.detail: No activity numbers on clickDrop images (the pop-out number is not on the image). Remove all dropboxes from the activity boxes — ONE dropbox at the bottom of the page. Intro copy supplied ('Below are activities. You can choose the activities you feel will enhance your learning…'). Explicit titles: Learn about… / Explain why… / Practise… / Compare … versus … / Do you think…? / Create … Each activity: text explaining what to do; media (video or image); an invitation to share with kaiako. Compare activities add a Venn-diagram prompt ('You may like to use a Venn diagram to compare') + a 'What is a Venn diagram?' button (video https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lnalI7eVQsQ&t=16s) + 'Here is an example of what your Venn diagram might look like.'

conventions.name: Dropbox copy + 'Upload to Dropbox' button
conventions.detail: Dropbox title 'Share your learning!'; body: 'When you have completed your chosen activities, upload your photos, videos or voice recordings to show your kaiako. If you require a specific media uploaded to the dropbox use the corresponding icon. When there is more than one type of media students can upload, use the generic dropbox button.'

conventions.name: End-of-page 'invitation to move forward' alerts (supplied copy)
conventions.detail: Exploratory: 'Ka pai! You've completed this lesson about _____ where we started to explore __learning intention__. Choose which lesson you would like to explore next! Click on the back button below to return to the introduction page and choose your next activity.' Lesson-by-lesson: 'Ka pai! You've completed lesson _, where we started to explore __learning intention__. Now let's try lesson _.' End of module: 'Ka pai! You have completed this module. We hope you enjoyed your learning. Discuss with your kaiako what topic you might like to explore next!'

conventions.name: XLP unique supervisor overview
conventions.detail: XLP = Learning Partner Toolkits (for supervisors) — unique overview, not the full ākonga-facing overview.

conventions.name: Standard LS overview (non-XLP)
conventions.detail: Overview tab: UKD, LI and SC. Information tab: Planning your time + What do I need to get started. Standards tab: Assessment for learning + the standards. Whakataukī in Te Reo AND English. First line: 'This module is called …' with an audio hover trigger over the Te Reo word. Second body text: purpose of the module. Media: video or photo. Then the move-forward prompt (text prompt if ordered lesson-by-lesson; if exploratory: 'Below are options you can select from. You can choose to start anywhere.' + buttons to pages, with the smaller words ('Move', 'Eat', etc.) removed).

Head-only dialogue strips: col-md-2 paddingR image + col-md-10 align-self-center bubble (closing variant col-md-3 + col-md-9); speaker-on-right rows REVERSE the column order but the image column STILL takes paddingR — a deliberate HPE exception to CL-0055, scoped to HPE head-only dialogue strips ONLY. The FIRST CL-0001/constraint-1 exception permitting deletion of writer characters: Unicode Extended_Pictographic grapheme CLUSTERS (base + VS15/16, skin tones, ZWJ sequences, keycap marks, flag pairs) are removed from the rendered page, EXCEPT the ledger's exempt ticks & crosses ✅✓✔☑✗✘❌❎ (kept cluster-whole — a VS16 is never orphan-stripped off a kept tick) and the ONE measured extension, the maths operators ✖➗➕➖ (meaning-bearing; gold keeps ✖ x12; ✖ is a cross by form — the ledger's own ☑ inclusion proves box/heavy variants count). EP arrow emoji (➡⬅⬆⬇⮕) become PLAIN arrows (→←↑↓) instead of deletions — gold's own treatment (TEDC402 ships the writer's 'input🡪process🡪output' as 'input→process→output'); a keycap digit keeps its digit. A run of 2+ consecutive plain

lines PREFIXED by a would-be-deleted cluster becomes ONE

    /
  • (lead dropped); a lone one stays a

    ; in-prose removals get spacing normalised; a

    the strip EMPTIED is dropped whole. Disclosure: ONE visible note per affected page at the first removal — 'Red Flag: Emoji have been removed from this content per the no-emoji rule. Ticks and crosses are retained.' (the r219 scheme's form, class cv2-note = gate-excluded; a header/menu first-removal relocates to the body top, the r203 rule). OUT OF SCOPE by the Unicode property (measured decisions): the checkbox/ballot family ☐☒□🗹 (bilingual checklists + printable tick-sheets; the r212 checklist→bullet stays the reo-menu machinery), 🖵 phonics sound-boxes, 🡪, plain →←, typographic ►●◦, private-use chars. CONTAINMENTS: cv2-interactive hand-off boxes, cv2-note/cv2-comment quotes, the acks block (verbatim oEmbed titles + the converter's own ❗ ack-todo markers), tag attributes, the {CODE}_interactives.txt hand-off, self-reflection emoji IMAGES (img assets) — all untouched.
rules.overrides_gold_notes: The gold library largely ALREADY lives the rule (CEDT104 gold ships 1 emoji from a WT of 279; ARFUN02 0 of 187) — but gold KEEPS emoji at named sites the rule strips: TEDC402's five feelings-scale faces (😎🙂😐😬🤯 in built tabs panes), OSBY301-class scattered singles (~18), TRR109/110 + XGF9001 + BLL120/252 + XDLS908, and gold keeps ➡/🡪 arrow FORMS where the converter now ships the plain-arrow form (TEDC401). All are INTENTIONAL CL-0051 overrides — record, never chase. THE WATCH CLASS: MXDI201/ENGS102-style emoji-as-CONTENT (vocab/description cards where the emoji IS the referent — gold keeps ~220 on MXDI201) currently lives INSIDE cv2-interactive dumps on the converter side, so the strip cannot touch it TODAY; any future widget-build round that renders that content live must re-visit the carve-out question with this entry as the evidence pointer (outputs/_measure_emoji.py, the r234 censuses).
rules.v2_home: Data Input_Doc_Rules.emoji_strip (exempt list VERBATIM from the ledger + exempt_extensions.maths_operators + arrow_map, all data-editable); engine ListsAndRuns.EmojiStrip (the r213 LinkTextDisplay post-pass seam — runs AFTER all tag machinery, so the ✅-glued [TITLE BAR] fences (r230 OSSC), the r192 ✅[Tile] delimiters, the r169 title splits and the 🔴 red-run sentinels are untouchable BY CONSTRUCTION); wired in PageAssembler before LinkTextDisplay, stopping at the acks block. Measurement: outputs/_measure_emoji.py (both rendered corpora, 8-shard) + _probe_emojistrip.cjs (behaviour/toggle/fence legs) + _probe_r234_toggle.cjs (corpus-scale EMOJISTRIP_OFF byte-identity vs the r232 manifest).

rules.name:
A writer's explicit go-to-journal button ships the templated

Go to your journal

inside the activity box
rules.rule:
A [button] whose EXPLICIT label folds to 'go to (your) journal' — or the alias-typed [go to journal]/[journal button] span — renders as the design team's templated

Go to your journal

INSIDE the open activity box (a bundle-owned activity absorbs a directly-following such button into the box before it closes), never as a green
. A button carrying a URL, and a bare [Button] whose label came only from the journal_label_default, keep the existing button behaviour.
rules.overrides_gold_notes: The gold library is ERA-MIXED: <h4 class=goJournal> ×568 / 57 modules vs <div class=button>Go to journal ×1,052 / 104 modules, MIXED within most subjects (no group discriminator — measured round 239). The developer's SCCH302 feedback names the h4 as the design team's CURRENT convention, so this is a forward-looking overrides-gold rule: at the Round-6 (Dev-Feedback chain) full regeneration, divergence from a button-form gold at a go-to-journal site is an INTENTIONAL design-team override — never chase it back toward the gold; gates judged net of exactly this named delta (WT population ~1,051 occ / 111 modules).

rules.name: Every content image ships alt text (verified iStock API title > URL-slug Title-Case) + loading="lazy"
rules.rule: A content image's alt attribute is populated from the asset's title — the VERIFIED iStock API title when the *_istock-acks.txt map covers the id, else the URL slug Title-Cased (the verified 98% slug-is-title rule); nothing derivable → alt stays empty (never invent a description). Every content also carries loading="lazy". Applies to the Mode-P visible placeholder, the Mode-P commented-out real reference (the tag the developer copies out), and the Mode-D direct , on free-body AND table-cell images.
rules.overrides_gold_notes: The gold library is ERA-MIXED: alt populated on 73% of 29,202 gold images (much of it hand-typed editorial text like 'Beautification image'), loading="lazy" on only 24% (older modules predate the convention) — measured round 240. The developer's SCCH302 feedback names the iStock API title + loading="lazy" as the design team's CURRENT convention, so this is a forward-looking overrides-gold rule: at the Round-6 (Dev-Feedback chain) full regeneration, alt/loading divergence from gold at any content image is an INTENTIONAL design-team override — never chase it back toward the gold (neither toward gold's hand-typed alts nor toward its lazy-less era); gates judged net of exactly this named delta (blast = every image-carrying page).

rules.name: No col-md-8 nested directly inside another col-md-8

rules.name: Speech-bubble image-column padding sides: left -> paddingR, right -> paddingL
rules.rule: A built speech-bubble image column takes inner-side padding: left-positioned image -> paddingR, right-positioned -> paddingL; never mirror a sibling that pads both sides the same. HPE head-only dialogue strips are the ONE scoped exception (paddingR both sides, CL-0067 — see the 14.8 family).
